contentHtml:
SOUTH AFRICA—President Cyril Ramaphosa, accompanied by Minister of Health Aaron Motsoaledi, has officially inaugurated the new King Nyabela Hospital in Mpumalanga, marking a significant milestone in South Africa’s efforts to strengthen public healthcare services.

Named after King Nyabela of the Ndzundza-Ndebele people, the 220-bed district hospital will provide essential healthcare services to more than 240,000 residents of the Steve Tshwete Local Municipality.

Speaking at the opening ceremony, Ramaphosa described healthcare as a fundamental human right that enables every citizen to live with dignity.

He noted that South Africa’s Constitution guarantees everyone access to healthcare services and requires the state to take reasonable measures, within available resources, to progressively realize this right.

According to the president, the completion of King Nyabela Hospital demonstrates the government’s commitment to expanding access to quality healthcare across the country.

Comprehensive healthcare services

The newly commissioned hospital offers a broad range of inpatient and outpatient services designed to meet the healthcare needs of the surrounding communities.

Its inpatient facilities include surgical, medical, paediatric, antenatal, postnatal, neonatal and high-care wards, supported by three operating theatres and a modern accident and emergency department.

Outpatient services include a pharmacy, tuberculosis (TB) and HIV management, dentistry, eye care, dietetics and nutrition, occupational therapy, physiotherapy, social work, mental health services and medical male circumcision, among other essential healthcare programs.

Ramaphosa said the extensive range of services reflects the government’s vision of comprehensive healthcare, which extends beyond treating illness.

He explained that quality healthcare also focuses on disease prevention, early diagnosis, long-term management of medical conditions and promoting healthy lives from childhood through old age.

He added that comprehensive care addresses both physical and mental well-being while supporting patients throughout every stage of life.

Strengthening National Health Insurance

The president also reaffirmed the government’s commitment to implementing the National Health Insurance (NHI), describing it as a key step toward achieving universal health coverage.

He said the NHI aims to ensure that access to healthcare no longer depends on where people live or their financial circumstances.

Under the NHI framework, the government will establish a centralized national insurance fund that will purchase healthcare services from both public and private healthcare providers.

Ramaphosa said the system is intended to give all South Africans access to the full range of quality healthcare services they need without facing financial hardship.

He emphasized that the success of the NHI will depend on effective governance, strong leadership, a skilled healthcare workforce, consistently high standards of service delivery and uninterrupted access to medicines.

Commitment to accountability and quality care

Ramaphosa stressed that all hospitals and clinics commissioned under the NHI programme must be completed on schedule and within approved budgets. He noted that King Nyabela Hospital met both targets, demonstrating that major public health infrastructure projects can be delivered efficiently.

The president also reiterated the government’s determination to eliminate corruption, fraud and waste in the procurement of healthcare infrastructure, medical supplies and services.

While acknowledging progress in recovering stolen funds and prosecuting suspected offenders, he said authorities remain committed to strengthening accountability across the health sector.

Ramaphosa concluded by recognizing the dedication of healthcare professionals, noting that although hospitals are built with bricks and mortar, their true strength comes from the doctors, nurses and other healthcare workers who continue serving patients despite challenging conditions.
